Text: The order recites that disputes exist between the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad Company and certain other carriers designated in a list A attached to the order, carriers under Federal management, and certain workers represented by the seventeen cooperating (non-operating) railway labor organizations designated in a list B attached to the order, and that the President had assumed possession, control and operation of the carriers' transportation systems through the Secretary of the Army under Executive Order No. 10155 of August 25, 1950. Acting under the Constitution and the laws, including section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the disputes; states that nothing in the order is to be construed to derogate from the authority of the Secretary of the Army under Executive Order No. 10155 (the order under which the President had assumed possession of these carriers' transportation systems through the Secretary of the Army); it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; permits the board, to the extent it deems necessary or desirable, to make separate and independent findings with respect to each carrier involved; and directs that, in performing its functions under the order, the board comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended. It contains no sentence imposing a status-quo standstill on the carriers or employees.
